service.name: Live band karaoke
service.serviceType: Live band karaoke for company parties, after-parties and private events
service.description: A live band that plays 80s and 90s hits as a party band and hands the microphone to guests who want to sing, with lyrics on a screen and a host, for company holiday parties, sales kickoffs, after-parties and private events across Denver and Colorado.

faqs.a: No. The band plays a full set of 80s and 90s hits on its own, sung out front, so the night works as a party even if the mic never leaves the stage, and the host never puts anyone on the spot. The first singers are almost always a pair or a group, and once two or three songs have gone well, the list fills on its own.

faqs.q: How does a guest get on the list?
faqs.a: The songbook is printed for the tables and shown on the screen. A guest picks a song and gives the host their name, and the host keeps a paper sign-up list and calls each singer up. There's no app and nothing to download, and two or three colleagues can go up together on one song.

faqs.q: How is this different from a karaoke DJ?
faqs.a: With a backing track the singer is on their own. With a band, the tempo follows the singer, the band keeps the song going if somebody loses the verse, a second voice comes in on the chorus, and the song ends when it should. The words are on a screen either way.

faqs.q: How many people get a turn?
faqs.a: About six to ten guest songs fit in an hour, so at a party of two hundred most people sing along from the floor. If the list is still long when the booked time ends, you can add another half hour on the night at the same rate as the rest of the evening.
The person booking. Say when you book whether the songs run clean or as recorded, and the host keeps to it on the night.

The same band can play dinner first at a level the tables talk across, then turn up when the program ends and the karaoke starts. From there it's as loud as a party band, with its own monitors so the singer can hear themselves. If your venue has a sound limit, give us the number and it stays under it.

The band and the host, sound support that's the right size for the venue, two lyric screens (one facing the singer and one facing the crowd), the printed songbook, an announcement microphone for remarks and a raffle, and the certificate of insurance and W-9 your office needs.

faqs.q: What does the venue need to provide?
faqs.a: For the four-piece, a performance area of about 14 by 10 feet, two dedicated 20-amp circuits, 90 minutes to set up before the first set, and a venue contact for setup and sound check. The bigger band's footprint is on the technical page.
